attrs.evidence: Lineage relies on prior receipt CONTENTS — `invariants.before` is checked against the parent's `after`, and the delta is computed against the parent's manifest — while nothing bound those contents. A parent receipt is writable JSON; editing one after its child was written left every gate green. A child cannot hash itself, but it can hash every parent, which turns the chain into a content-linked history without waiting for signatures. MUT-PARENT-RECEIPT-EDIT alters a parent receipt and leaves the child untouched, and check-lineage §5 refuses.
attrs.gap: This is content-linking, NOT authentication. Nothing signs a receipt, nothing timestamps one, and an editor who changes a parent may simply update the child's recorded digest too — the chain then remains internally consistent and says nothing about who wrote it or when. That is FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH and it is open. The binding is worth having anyway: it makes an isolated edit fail loudly, which is the common case.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §9. Hash chaining, as in a Merkle-linked log; in-toto link chains verified against an intended sequence.
attrs.statement: A child receipt binds the sha256 of its parent receipt's bytes, so the chain of named JSON files is content-linked and a parent edited after its child breaks verification.
